prospect.name: Jeff Honigstock
prospect.occupation: Not established — commutes to work; formerly a social worker in his twenties. Uses a concierge doctor and holds three gym memberships alongside a home gym and a Tonal.
prospect.family_status: Married 22 years; 15-year-old son turning 15 the day after the call
prospect.training_background: Previously trained twice a week with an advanced kettlebell instructor at over $100 a session and got strong results, but stopped on cost. Built a gym in his basement and has never used it — his son does. Owns a Tonal, kettlebells and a jump rope. Enjoys yoga and golf, plays basketball with his son. Has not trained meaningfully for roughly three months.
prospect.medical: Diagnosed high blood pressure and borderline type 2 diabetes, both on medication, under the care of a concierge doctor who has instructed him to walk two miles a day. Coming off surgery for a distal biceps tear at the elbow — a 'popeye arm' — followed by six months of rehabilitation. Reports ADHD. Reports poor sleep. Cannot run a 13-minute mile and is exhausted after walking a mile. Stated hope of eliminating his medications.

The rep referenced a cheaper alternative product but did not describe it: 'If it's a no, because of the money only, let me know, because there is other things, but you are on a time constraint, so I can't run you through it right now.'

outcome.next_step: Rep calls at approximately 7:30am the following morning; prospect to give a yes or no after discussing the numbers with his wife

notable.note: The most medically loaded call in the batch and the one where the clinical omission is starkest. The prospect disclosed diagnosed hypertension, borderline diabetes, active medication, a concierge doctor who has given him a specific exercise instruction he is not following, and recent surgery for a torn biceps tendon at the elbow. The rep's response to the entire disclosure was 'I get it. I have it' and a comment about winter gyms. The prospect also said he expects to eliminate his medications and was not corrected. Separately: the setter 'Sophia', whom the prospect had been messaging and believed to be a person, is an AI — disclosed only because the prospect asked how large the company was.

quality.notes: Severe and systematic — the prospect's label 'JeffHonigstock' carries most of the rep's opening turns and much of the pitch, including the $6,000 price reveal at 00:47:25, while the rep's label carries several of the prospect's answers. Roles resolved entirely from content. The prospect ended the call abruptly for an 11am commitment, so the pricing conversation is cut off mid-sequence.
